plan.name: Bind Python observations to executed application code
plan.summary: Complete the directly callable Python application adapter by executing configured drivers and collecting sampled initial states and transitions from actual selected calls, using the gate-owned functional and instance read-back interfaces specified by the acceptance tests. Preserve staged application bytes, immutable dependency reuse, controlled offline execution, raw runtime-test outcomes and the public gate rejections, while rejecting substituted lifecycles, unsupported bindings, incomplete evidence, stale inputs and replayed output. Exercise both accepted forms and the refusal contract through actual Python, including the opt-in Docker suite with the unchanged lifecycle component, surrounding application entry points, resources, sibling imports and installed wheels. Update SPEC.md and README.md with the complete interface, examples, supported invocation and read-back forms, failure behavior, raw sampled outputs and session reuse, citing the recorded foundations and #313's ratified child plan; TLC checking, report attribution and public admission remain subsequent work. Merger work is to record the new observation/execution policy and dependencies, record and cite the preceding session policy if it is still absent as on this baseline, and post passing output from INVARIANT_PYTHON_APPLICATION_EXECUTION_REAL=1 go test ./internal/verify -run '^TestPythonApplicationExecution' -count=1 -timeout 30m on the final head; the build cannot edit decisions, pinned statements or ratified locks, and unavailable Docker/network checks alone do not require repair.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionBoundObservations
tests.says: Actual Python drivers call surrounding application entry points and return exact initial/pre/post state read-backs bound to the selected staged function or method, driver, invocation, ordered calls and distinct instances, with deterministic repeated and relocated results and one selected image.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionRejectsUnboundObservations
tests.says: After demonstrating successful bound execution, actual Python rejects unused, import-only, unexecuted, wrong-symbol, replaced and substituted lifecycles, wrong initial/pre/post states, cross-instance and closed-run reuse, unsupported readers, missing/malformed/empty output, and import/runtime failures without accepted observations or changes to original bytes.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionKeepsRuntimeOutcomesIndependent
tests.says: Successful driver evidence never turns independently observed failed, skipped, errored or unexecuted required tests into passing checks, changes their records, or invents assertions or test outcomes.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionObservationFreshness
tests.says: Real Python output cannot be replayed into another execution of the same invocation or another invocation, and input or trusted-runner changes before or during execution invalidate observations without resolving dependencies again or changing originals.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionObservationsReal
tests.says: The opt-in real Docker suite executes both binding forms, all negative drivers, freshness failures and independent runtime outcomes, with standard-library and recursive requirements/constraints sessions and real wheel evidence; explicit opt-in fails on missing prerequisites instead of skipping.
